zh.principle: **协议**：DNSSEC 域名安全（DNS Security Extensions）。摘要一句话说清扩展对象：「The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) add data origin authentication and data integrity to the Domain Name System.」本文件是介绍与需求文档，新记录与协议改动由配套文档族规定。
zh.why: §1 同时给出能力与不自称的能力：「The DNS security extensions provide origin authentication and integrity protection for DNS data, as well as a means of public key distribution.These extensions do not provide confidentiality.」即补齐的是来源与完整性，机密性被排除在设计之外。
zh.used: §3 列出协议改动：「DNSSEC adds four new resource record types: Resource Record Signature (RRSIG), DNS Public Key (DNSKEY), Delegation Signer (DS), and Next Secure (NSEC).It also adds two new message header bits: Checking Disabled (CD) and Authenticated Data (AD).」验证起点由 §2 的术语定义给出：「Trust Anchor: A configured DNSKEY RR or DS RR hash of a DNSKEY RR.」
zh.broken: 自陈的边界有两处：§4 说明「Accordingly, DNSSEC is not designed to provide confidentiality, access control lists, or other means of differentiating between inquirers.」；可用性同样没有承诺——「DNSSEC provides no protection against denial of service attacks.」并指出验证签名会给解析器与权威服务器带来新的一类拒绝服务面。
zh.history:

en.principle: **Protocol**: DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC 域名安全). The abstract states what the extensions add: "The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) add data origin authentication and data integrity to the Domain Name System." This document is the introduction and requirements; the new records and protocol modifications are specified by the companion document set.
en.why: Section 1 gives both the capability and the disclaimer: "The DNS security extensions provide origin authentication and integrity protection for DNS data, as well as a means of public key distribution. These extensions do not provide confidentiality." Origin and integrity are added; confidentiality is excluded by design.
en.used:
Section 3 lists the protocol changes: "DNSSEC adds four new resource record types: Resource Record Signature (RRSIG), DNS Public Key (DNSKEY), Delegation Signer (DS), and Next Secure (NSEC). It also adds two new message header bits: Checking Disabled (CD) and Authenticated Data (AD)." The starting point is defined in §2: "Trust Anchor: A configured DNSKEY RR or DS RR hash of a DNSKEY RR."

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken: Two limits are stated outright: §4 says "Accordingly, DNSSEC is not designed to provide confidentiality, access control lists, or other means of differentiating between inquirers.", and availability is not claimed either — "DNSSEC provides no protection against denial of service attacks." — with signature verification itself creating a new denial-of-service surface.
en.history: The RFC 4033 header lists R. Arends (Telematica Instituut), R. Austein (ISC), M. Larson (VeriSign), D. Massey (Colorado State University) and S. Rose (NIST), Category: Standards Track, March 2005; the same block lists nine obsoleted documents starting with 2535 and nine updated ones starting with 1034 and 1035, and since those lists interleave with the author column in the text file they are paraphrased rather than quoted.

zh: RRSIG：资源记录集的签名记录。
DS：委派签名者，把父区指向子区密钥。
NSEC：否定存在的旧证明机制。
CD 与 AD 位：验证跳过开关与已验证标记。
信任锚：解析器开始验证的配置起点。
en: RRSIG: the signature over a resource record set.
DS: the delegation signer linking a parent to a child key.
CD and AD bits: the validation opt-out and the validated marker.
Trust anchor: the configured key a resolver starts validation from.
